text: Reputation in the underlying system is domain-specific and strictly non-transferable: bound to the holder's identity, earned only through validated work, and incapable of sale, loan or transfer.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights? (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7596939

isBasedOn.name: Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights?

abstract: Should intelligent agents have legal rights? This Article sets that question aside and asks a smaller one that matters more in practice. An intelligent agent that earns a reputation record has something to lose.

additionalProperty.name: supporting_quote
additionalProperty.value: Reputation is held as tokens specific to a domain of expertise (Calcaterra, Kaal, and Andrei 2018, p. 5), bound to the holder's identity, and cannot be sold, lent, or transferred. It is earned only through validated work.
